# Planning Our First AI Feature: Auto-Generated Product Description and Image

## The Problem We Want to Solve

Let's look at the **Add Product** form in our e-commerce app. Filling in fields like product name, brand, category, price, stock, and release date is quick and easy. But there are two fields that take much more effort:

1. **Description** — writing a good product description takes time and thought
2. **Product Image** — you need to have (or create) a suitable image to upload

Wouldn't it be great if the AI could handle both of these for us?

### What We Want to Achieve

```
User fills in: Product Name, Brand, Category (basic info)
        |
        v
Click "Generate" --> AI writes a product description automatically
        |
        v
Click "Generate Image" --> AI creates a matching product image automatically
```

This would save a lot of time when adding new products — instead of manually writing descriptions and sourcing images, the AI does the heavy lifting, and the user can still edit the generated result if needed.

## Two Places That Need Updating

To make this work, we need changes in **two separate parts** of the project:

1. **Frontend (UI)** → needs buttons/actions to trigger these AI generation features
2. **Backend** → needs the actual capability (API endpoints) to generate the description and image using Spring AI

> The good news: a version of the **frontend UI** with these buttons **already exists** and is provided as part of the course resources — so we don't need to build the frontend from scratch. We just need to focus on building the **backend** functionality to make these buttons actually work.

## Setting Up the New Frontend Version

This updated frontend is a **separate project folder** (distinct from the earlier frontend version we explored) — something like `ecom-frontend-ai` (an AI-feature-enabled version of the same e-commerce UI).

### Running It

Just like before, setting up this frontend involves the same familiar steps:

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

**Explanation:**

- `npm install` → installs the required packages (safe to run again even if `node_modules` already exists, just to be sure nothing is missing)
- `npm run dev` → starts the frontend development server

> **Note:** The **backend** stays exactly the same as before — only the **frontend** here is a different/updated version, specifically built to support these new AI-related buttons.

## Exploring the Updated "Add Product" Page

The new frontend's Add Product form looks slightly different, but the core idea remains: you enter basic product details (name, brand, category, etc.), and now you'll also see:

- A **"Generate" button** next to the Description field (marked optional, since it *can* be filled manually too, but can now also be auto-generated)
- A **"Generate Image" button**, which becomes enabled only **after** a description exists

### Testing What's Already There (and What's Missing)

1. Filling in basic details (example: product name "Mass Phone," brand, category "Mobile") works fine, as expected
2. Clicking **"Generate"** (for the description) currently results in an error: *"Failed to generate description. Try again."*

### Why Does This Fail?

> This isn't a UI bug — the frontend is correctly sending a request to the backend, but **the backend doesn't have any endpoint yet to handle it.** If you check the browser's network/error details, you'd see something like: *"Request method POST is not supported"* — confirming that no matching backend endpoint currently exists for this action.

3. The **"Generate Image"** button is initially **disabled** — this is intentional, since generating a relevant image makes more sense once there's at least a basic description available to base the image on. Once a description is typed or generated, this button becomes enabled.

## The Plan Going Forward

We'll build this feature **step by step**, rather than trying to implement everything at once:

```
Step 1: Build the backend capability for generating a product DESCRIPTION
        (make the "Generate" button for description actually work)

Step 2: Build the backend capability for generating a product IMAGE
        (make the "Generate Image" button actually work)
```

## What's Next

In the upcoming topics, we'll start with the **description generation** feature — building the actual backend endpoint using Spring AI, so that clicking "Generate" on the frontend successfully returns an AI-written product description. After that, we'll move on to image generation.

## Quick Summary

| Concept | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Goal | Let the AI auto-generate a product's description and image, based on basic product details entered by the user |
| Two places to update | The frontend (buttons/UI to trigger generation) and the backend (actual AI-powered endpoints) |
| New frontend version | A separate, already-built frontend project (provided in course resources) that includes the necessary "Generate" buttons |
| Current status | The frontend buttons exist, but generation fails because the backend has no matching endpoints yet |
| Order of implementation | First build description generation, then build image generation |

## Practice Questions

**Q1: What two fields in the "Add Product" form were identified as time-consuming, and therefore good candidates for AI assistance?**
A: The product Description and the Product Image.

**Q2: Why did clicking "Generate" for the description result in an error, even though a new frontend with the button already exists?**
A: Because the backend doesn't yet have an endpoint to handle this request — the frontend correctly sends the request, but there's nothing on the backend to accept and process it (resulting in an error like "Request method POST is not supported").

**Q3: Why is the "Generate Image" button initially disabled on the form?**
A: Because it only becomes enabled once a product description exists (either typed manually or AI-generated), since the image generation is meant to be based on that description.

**Q4: What is the planned order for implementing these two AI features?**
A: First, implement description generation; then, implement image generation.

**Q5: Did the backend project need to change for this new frontend version to run?**
A: No — the backend stays the same for now; only a different, updated frontend project (with the new AI-related buttons) is being used.
